decisions.reason: As a newly launched safety shoe line in the firm’s core category, it fits the company’s strategy of continuous innovation and is unlikely to be withdrawn so soon without evidence of clear market failure.

The comfort insole complements the main footwear range well and supports cross-selling, though as an accessory with less visible prominence it faces a somewhat higher rationalization risk than core shoes.

The supportive insole also fits the company’s protective-footwear system offer, but overlap with other insole products makes it slightly more exposed to portfolio cleanup if demand is weaker than expected.
The ergonomic safety shoe series appears strategically important, and having its own page suggests a strong commercial focus consistent with the firm’s emphasis on innovation and tailored solutions.

Firefighter and rescue boots serve a specialized professional segment that matches the firm’s protective expertise, but the niche nature of the market makes them a bit more vulnerable than mainstream safety footwear.
The moulded insole was prominent enough to appear on the home page, indicating active marketing support and a good fit with the firm’s broader footwear and service proposition.
